title: drcTMB: dose-response models with TMB
text: drcTMB fits nonlinear dose-response models maximum likelihood Template Model Builder (TMB). interface resembles drm() drc package. TMB’s automatic differentiation Laplace approximation extend models beyond nonlinear regression: non-normal responses (binomial, counts, proportions, time--event data), covariates random effects every parameter curve, correlated residuals variance functions, priors, Bayesian benchmark doses. Effective doses benchmark doses, standard errors confidence intervals, available models. examples use data sets drcTMB, package drcData, nlme; plots use ggplot2.
code: library(drcTMB) library(ggplot2)

title: drcTMB: dose-response models with TMB
text: drmTMB() takes formula response ~ dose, data, name model function argument model. models share parameter names b1 b5: models use parameters differently: michaelismenten, asymptoticregression, exponentialdecay, gamma: b1 response dose zero b2 asymptote high doses. braincousens, cedergreen (hormesis): b5 size stimulation low doses, see Hormesis. exponential, power: upper asymptote, see Benchmark doses. available models : formulas models given Appendix. argument start gives starting values, name, fix (TRUE/FALSE) fixes parameters starting values. Parameters model use, b5 Weibull models, fixed automatically.

text: predict() gives fitted curve. interval = "confidence", adds standard errors confidence intervals mean response (delta method). interval = "prediction", intervals new observation include residual variation. result data frame columns fit, se.fit, lwr upr.  Alternatively, intervals can come parametric bootstrap: bootstrap() simulates new responses fitted model fits model . bootstrap sample can reused predict() confint().
code: # the controls (conc = 0) are drawn at a small concentration on the log axis ryegrass$cplot <- ifelse(ryegrass$conc == 0, 0.25, ryegrass$conc) ndata <- data.frame(conc = exp(seq(log(0.25), log(30), length.out = 100)))  ci <- predict(mod, newdata = ndata, interval = "confidence") pri <- predict(mod, newdata = ndata, interval = "prediction") head(ci, 3) #>        fit    se.fit      lwr      upr #> 1 7.841681 0.1988884 7.428069 8.255292 #> 2 7.839940 0.1983205 7.427510 8.252370 #> 3 7.837979 0.1977000 7.426839 8.249118  bands <- rbind(cbind(ndata, ci, interval = "95% confidence interval"),                cbind(ndata, pri, interval = "95% prediction interval")) ggplot(bands, aes(x = conc)) +   geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lwr, ymax = upr, fill = interval), alpha = 0.3) +   geom_line(data = cbind(ndata, ci), aes(y = fit), colour = "blue") +   geom_point(data = ryegrass, aes(x = cplot, y = rootl)) +   scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.25, 1, 3, 10, 30), labels = c("0", "1", "3", "10", "30")) +   scale_fill_manual(values = c("steelblue", "grey60")) +   labs(x = "Concentration (log scale)", y = "Root length (cm)", fill = NULL) +   theme_bw() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom") bs <- bootstrap(mod, nsim = 200, seed = 1) head(predict(mod, newdata = ndata, interval = "confidence", boot = bs), 3) #>        fit    se.fit      lwr      upr #> 1 7.841681 0.1888989 7.425923 8.168309 #> 2 7.839940 0.1883664 7.425174 8.164460 #> 3 7.837979 0.1877909 7.424313 8.160199

text: ed() estimates effective doses response levels respLev. effective dose ED p dose response changed p% difference asymptote low doses (control) asymptote high doses. Confidence intervals confint() profile likelihood intervals default. Simultaneous confidence intervals follow package multcomp. gaussian models without random effects, residual degrees freedom give multivariate t quantiles (df.residual() NULL otherwise, multcomp uses normal distribution). type = "absolute", respLev gives values response instead, ed() estimates doses curve reaches , root length 2, 4 6 cm. doses depend asymptotes well, included standard errors.
code: (effdose <- ed(mod, respLev = c(25, 50, 75))) #> Effective dose estimates: #>  #>        Estimate Std.Error #> 25:lf1     2.09     0.187 #> 50:lf1     3.26     0.196 #> 75:lf1     5.09     0.421 confint(effdose) #> Computing profile confidence intervals ... #>           2.5 %   97.5 % #> 25:lf1 1.719261 2.496939 #> 50:lf1 2.879163 3.703885 #> 75:lf1 4.332774 6.110914 library(multcomp) linfct <- diag(3) rownames(linfct) <- c("ED25", "ED50", "ED75") confint(glht(effdose, linfct = linfct, df = df.residual(mod))) #>  #>   Simultaneous Confidence Intervals #>  #> Fit: NULL #>  #> Quantile = 2.4931 #> 95% family-wise confidence level #>   #>  #> Linear Hypotheses: #>           Estimate lwr    upr    #> ED25 == 0 2.0918   1.6264 2.5573 #> ED50 == 0 3.2634   2.7737 3.7530 #> ED75 == 0 5.0910   4.0408 6.1412 ed(mod, respLev = c(2, 4, 6), type = "absolute") #> Effective dose estimates: #>  #>         Estimate Std.Error #> y=2:lf1     5.04     0.414 #> y=4:lf1     3.22     0.173 #> y=6:lf1     2.03     0.156

code: data(daphnids) d48 <- subset(daphnids, time == "48h") dmod <- drmTMB(cbind(no, total - no) ~ dose, data = d48, model = "loglogistic", family = "binomial",                start = c(b1 = 0, b2 = 1, b4 = 1000, b5 = 0), fix = c(b1 = TRUE, b2 = TRUE, b5 = TRUE)) dmod #> Call: #> drmTMB(form = cbind(no, total - no) ~ dose, data = d48, start = c(b1 = 0,  #>     b2 = 1, b4 = 1000, b5 = 0), fix = c(b1 = TRUE, b2 = TRUE,  #>     b5 = TRUE), family = "binomial", model = "loglogistic") #>  #> Model:  loglogistic #> Family: binomial, identity link for the asymptotes #>  #> Coefficients: #> b3:(Intercept)  b4:(Intercept)   #>           1.85         1509.06   #> Fixed: b1:(Intercept) = 0, b2:(Intercept) = 1, b5:(Intercept) = 0 ndata <- data.frame(dose = exp(seq(3, log(22000), length.out = 100)), no = 0, total = 20) cib <- predict(dmod, newdata = ndata, interval = "confidence") pib <- predict(dmod, newdata = ndata, interval = "prediction", nsim = 2000, seed = 1)  ggplot(cbind(ndata, pib), aes(x = dose)) +   geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), fill = "grey60", alpha = 0.3) +   geom_ribbon(data = cbind(ndata, cib), aes(ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.4) +   geom_line(aes(y = fit), colour = "blue") +   geom_point(data = d48, aes(y = no/total)) +   scale_x_log10(breaks = c(100, 500, 2500, 10000)) +   labs(x = "Dose (log scale)", y = "Proportion of immobile daphnids",        subtitle = "Blue: 95% confidence interval; grey: 95% prediction interval for 20 daphnids") +   theme_bw()

code: dmodg <- drmTMB(cbind(no, total - no) ~ dose, data = daphnids,                 model = "loglogistic", family = "binomial",                 fform = b3 + b4 ~ 0 + time,                 start = c(b1 = 0, b2 = 1, b4 = 1000, b5 = 0), fix = c(b1 = TRUE, b2 = TRUE, b5 = TRUE)) dmodg #> Call: #> drmTMB(form = cbind(no, total - no) ~ dose, fform = b3 + b4 ~  #>     0 + time, data = daphnids, start = c(b1 = 0, b2 = 1, b4 = 1000,  #>     b5 = 0), fix = c(b1 = TRUE, b2 = TRUE, b5 = TRUE), family = "binomial",  #>     model = "loglogistic") #>  #> Model:  loglogistic #> Family: binomial, identity link for the asymptotes #>  #> Coefficients: #> b3:time24h  b3:time48h  b4:time24h  b4:time48h   #>      1.174       1.850    5134.036    1509.065   #> Fixed: b1:(Intercept) = 0, b2:(Intercept) = 1, b5:(Intercept) = 0 ndatag <- expand.grid(dose = exp(seq(3, log(22000), length.out = 100)),                       time = c("24h", "48h")) ndatag$pred <- predict(dmodg, newdata = ndatag)  ggplot(daphnids, aes(x = dose, y = no/total, colour = time)) +   geom_point() +   geom_line(data = ndatag, aes(y = pred)) +   scale_x_log10(breaks = c(100, 500, 2500, 10000)) +   labs(x = "Dose (log scale)", y = "Proportion of immobile daphnids", colour = "Time") +   theme_bw()

text: drcTMB fits nonlinear dose-response models maximum likelihood Template Model Builder (TMB). interface resembles drm() drc package, TMB’s automatic differentiation Laplace approximation extend models well beyond nonlinear regression: random effects, non-normal responses, covariates every parameter, correlated residuals priors, together effective doses benchmark doses .

title: Fitting Dose-Response Curves Using the Template Model Builder
text: Dose-response models: log-logistic, logistic, Weibull (two types), log-normal, Gompertz, gamma, multistage, Michaelis-Menten, asymptotic regression, hormesis models Brain-Cousens Cedergreen, threshold model NEC, substrate inhibition model Haldane, exponential power models PROAST BMDS. share parameter names b1 b5 (lower upper asymptote, steepness, location, asymmetry shape). Response distributions (family): gaussian, lognormal, binomial, beta-binomial, poisson, negative binomial, beta, time--event data (germination counts time intervals). Covariates parameters (fform), e.g. one ED50 treatment, links single parameters (parlink) whole curve (curvelink). Random effects parameters (rform), correlated random intercepts slopes nested grouping factors, lme4. Correlated residuals variance functions (correlation, variance): AR(1), continuous-time AR(1), compound symmetry spatial structures; power, exponential stratified variances, nlme. Inference: Wald, profile likelihood parametric bootstrap intervals; likelihood ratio, F bootstrap tests anova(); robust (sandwich) standard errors, also clustered data; confidence prediction intervals predict(); residual diagnostics plot(). Effective doses (ed()) peak hormesis curves (peak()), every curve model, simultaneous intervals ratios effective doses multcomp mratios. Benchmark doses (bmd()): excess additional risk, relative deviation standard deviation definitions, also random effects; model averaging AIC BIC weights bootstrap BMDLs (bmdma()). Bayesian benchmark doses: priors parameters BMD , marginal likelihoods Bayesian model averaging (bmdbayes()), default approach EFSA (2022) single call (bmdefsa()).

text: immobility daphnids recorded 24 48 hours. binomial model separate steepness b3 location b4 time compares two curves; asymptotes fixed 0 1, ED50s start dose 1000.  ed() estimates effective doses curve given newdata, covariance matrix, simultaneous intervals differences (multcomp::glht()) ratios (mratios::gsci.ratio()) follow, relative potency ED50 24 hours one 48 hours.

title: drcTMB 0.1.0
text: drmTMB() fits nonlinear dose-response models Template Model Builder: log-logistic, logistic, Weibull (two types), log-normal, Gompertz, Michaelis-Menten, asymptotic regression, gamma, multistage, threshold model nec, hormesis models Brain-Cousens Cedergreen, substrate inhibition model Haldane, exponential power models PROAST BMDS, constant model. Response distributions: gaussian, lognormal, binomial, beta-binomial, beta, poisson, negative binomial (nbinom1, nbinom2), time--event data (family = "event"). Covariates parameter (fform), random effects parameter syntax lme4 (rform), parameter links (parlink) links whole curve (curvelink). Correlated residuals (cor_ar1(), cor_car1(), cor_cs(), cor_exp(), cor_gaus(), cor_spher()) variance functions (var_power(), var_exp(), var_ident()) gaussian lognormal families. Priors parameters (prior, see ?priors), estimates posterior modes. Starting values linearised models grid search (drmTMBstart()); choice optimiser restart estimates (drmTMBcontrol()). Data sets package drcData, CRAN: chickweed, daphnids, earthworms, germination, lettuce, liver.tumor, ryegrass, S.alba, selenium, TCDD vinclozolin.
